verdict.rationale: LlamaParse's own docs describe Parse as a parser built for LLM pipelines that outputs clean markdown, text, or JSON, so the LLM-ready output part of the story is directly documented. Nothing in the evidence explicitly says repeated headers, footers, or other page furniture are stripped; 'clean' only implies it. One community user praised its handling of a complex layout. Missing for 10: documented removal of repeated headers/footers and page furniture, any configuration controls for noise stripping, hands-on corroboration of noise removal.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I get clean markdown/JSON designed for LLM consumption, with noise like repeated headers and page furniture stripped

citations.quote: Parse is an agentic document parser built for LLM pipelines—layout-aware OCR that turns PDFs, scans, tables, and charts into clean markdown, text, or JSON.
Turn PDFs, scans, or images into clean LLM-ready text
Parse converts PDFs, scans and Office files to markdown or JSON
